notes:
The leaf continues a programme for describing possible exterior actions of open subgroups Gamma of Gamma_Q on profinite fundamental groups and on further K(Pi,1) groups realizable by algebraic varieties. Modular varieties for algebraic curves are offered as an example. It proposes reconstructing smooth schemes, or their category, over fields of finite type over Q and more generally arbitrary fields by gluing, then discusses schemes locally of finite type and a category of fractions. These are the author's prospective claims, not proved on this leaf; no mathematical check was performed. Ink controls the readings: Gamma is unprimed, Pi has a capital angular form, surtout is live despite retracing, and tels remains masculine after topos was replaced by inserted variétés. The sign before un K remains explicitly doubtful, with a q-like glyph first and cancelled d/f and universal-sign alternatives; its cancellation state is also unresolved. The cancelled word retains égale first and égalant as an alternative. Quotation marks are paired raised ticks; loc has no stop, while gén., cat., and inv. retain their written stops. The last line ends with les, without completing the sentence. The author’s number 25 is at the head and is transcribed with mspage; the thinner bottom-left foliation 50 is a margin entry. There are no diagrams, drawings, or other margins. All C/H agreements and disagreements were read, including the two additions and both secure cancellations.

[Blind audit] All six differing crops were inspected, with the seven supplied details except the unnecessary B07 short-word detail. Preserve the visible fondamen-taux line-division hyphen. The first des gains a de alternative; question has no distinct final s and remains singular. Live surtout is retained: after the retraced surt- the next round letter is o, without the extra initial t needed for avant tout. The tiny post-là mark has a pointed left end and is now a doubtful left arrow with on as alternative; the reconstruction verb retains its primary conditional ending with a future-form alternative. De ceux-là remains clear from the x, detached hyphen, tall l and accented à, against the blind connexes. The full expression before un K was reread and the retraced sign is left explicitly unresolved, now with q primary and cancellation-state alternatives. Tout remains readable, while au gains du; the cancelled égale gains égalant. These are ink decisions, not grammatical completion. No mathematical check was performed.
